player.seasonOutlook: After signing a one-year deal with the Sun in 2025, rejoining the team that selected her with the first overall pick in the 2010 WNBA Draft, Charles announced her retirement ahead of the 2026 season. The veteran center played 15 seasons in the WNBA, averaging 17.7 points, 9.0 rebounds and 2.2 assists in 31.6 minutes per game, and she won the MVP award in 2012.

Cunningham missed the end of the 2025 campaign due to a torn MCL in her right knee and was an unrestricted free agent heading into 2026, but she'll remain with the Fever on a one-year deal. While the injury from last season isn't expected to impact her availability to start 2026, Cunningham has appeared in more than 31 regular-season games only once in her seven-year career. She's also averaged double-digit points per game only twice and never averaged more than 4.4 rebounds or 2.1 assists for an entire campaign. Cunningham's fantasy value is mostly tied to her defense -- she has recorded at least one steal per game in three of the last four seasons -- and three-point shooting, making nearly two made triples a night over the past four years.

After six seasons in Atlanta to begin her career, Billings has suited up for the Wings, Mercury and Valkyries over the past two seasons. The veteran center is a solid rebounder and defender, but it's unclear how impactful she can be moving forward. She made only 26 appearances (eight starts) for Golden State in 2025 while averaging 18.2 minutes per game. Billings was an unrestricted free agent ahead of the 2026 campaign and agreed to a contract with Indiana, where she should compete with Myisha Hines-Allen and Sophie Cunningham for minutes. Her fantasy value could be muted if she's forced to settle for a bench role, but her upside could rise considerably if she can consistently operate as a starter. She failed to post double-digit fantasy points only once when she played at least 20 minutes last season (13 games).

Wheeler proved she still had plenty left in the tank during her 2025 bounce-back campaign in Seattle, averaging 10.3 points, 3.3 assists, 2.7 rebounds and 1.3 steals across 25.6 minutes in all 44 regular-season games. She showed improved range from deep, knocking down 37.3 percent of her threes on a career-high 4.6 attempts per game. However, the mid-season acquisition of Brittney Sykes pushed Wheeler to the bench for the final stretch. She was an unrestricted free agent during the offseason and agreed to terms with the Sparks, where she may need to maintain a reserve role in 2026, especially after Los Angeles brought back Kelsey Plum while trading for Ariel Atkins. The steals production and three-point shooting give her category value in deeper leagues, but her game-to-game inconsistency remains a concern -- she fluctuated wildly between 20-point eruptions and scoreless outings in 2025. Wheeler is best viewed as a back-end roster option whose upside is tied to injuries or lineup shuffles ahead of her.

Parker-Tyus missed the final month of the 2024 campaign due to an ankle injury, she missed most of her first year with the Aces in 2025 after giving birth in July. She made just eight appearances for the Aces between the regular season and playoffs, averaging 3.5 points in 6.4 minutes per game. Despite her limited role, Parker-Tyus has had ample playing time for most of her career and could be poised for a bounce-back year in 2026. Across 25 regular-season appearances (11 starts) with Atlanta in 2024, she averaged 9.2 points and 4.8 rebounds in 19.7 minutes per game after averaging double-digit points and at least 20 minutes per game in each of her previous four seasons. Parker-Tyus re-signed with the Aces ahead of the 2026 campaign and could carve out a larger role during her second season with Las Vegas since she'll be able to work with the team during training camp and early-season action.

The No. 8 overall pick in the 2025 WNBA Draft, Rivers had a rollercoaster rookie season. She scored in double figures 17 times, averaging 13.4 points, 3.2 rebounds, 2.8 assists, 1.6 steals and 1.0 blocks in 29.8 minutes while posting 48/43/83 shooting splits. However, in her other 25 appearances, Rivers posted only 5.7 points, 2.5 rebounds and 2.6 assists a night. One thing that remained consistent throughout the entire campaign was her defense, which should give her a strong chance at carving out a starting role in 2026, especially after Marina Mabrey went to Toronto in the WNBA Expansion Draft. Rivers started 25 of her 42 appearances in 2025, so a full-time starting role wouldn't be surprising, though Connecticut also brought in Gianna Kneepkens in the first round of the 2026 WNBA Draft. However, from a fantasy perspective, Rivers' playing time will be key. She averaged 26.1 minutes per game in her first season, which was fourth on the team, but only one player saw more than 30 minutes per game (Mabrey). If the Sun are conservative with minutes again, Rivers may struggle to reach her upside in Year 2, but her defensive prowess gives her a strong fantasy floor.

Following two seasons with the Liberty, Vandersloot returned to Chicago in 2025. The 37-year-old improved upon her 2024 results early in the 2025 campaign, averaging 10.6 points, 5.3 assists and 3.1 rebounds in 27.3 minutes per game over her first seven appearances before suffering a season-ending torn ACL. Vandersloot is one of the league's all-time leading passers, ranking second on the all-time assists leaderboard, behind only Sue Bird. However, her output has declined slightly in recent years, as she's averaged just 5.0 assists per game over the past two seasons. Vandersloot re-signed with the Sky ahead of the 2026 season, and while she should have an opportunity to maintain a starting role in Chicago, she doesn't have quite as much fantasy upside as she did earlier in her career, as the team traded away Ariel Atkins but brought in Skylar Diggins this spring.

Sheldon opened last season in a significant role for the Sun before being traded to the Mystics in exchange for Aaliyah Edwards. An ankle injury ended up ruining her campaign, costing her the final 12 games of 2025, and Sheldon's role with her new team was never quite able to become defined as a result. Overall, Sheldon averaged 7.5 points, 1.9 rebounds, 1.9 assists and 0.9 steals in 23.6 minutes per contest across 28 regular-season games for Connecticut and two for Washington. She'll have yet another change of scenery in 2026 after being traded to the Sky for a first-round pick. Chicago's valuation on Sheldon's talent appears to be high, but she'll have to compete with Skylar Diggins, Courtney Vandersloot and DiJonai Carrington for playing time in the Sky backcourt, which makes Sheldon a somewhat risky fantasy option.

Following a lack of opportunities in 2022 and 2023, Sims has experienced a resurgence in production over the past two seasons between the Wings, Sparks and Fever. Across 48 regular-season appearances (38 starts), she averaged 11.8 points, 4.5 assists and 2.3 rebounds in 29.0 minutes per game. Despite moving between the three teams, Sims displayed ample fantasy upside with consistent playing time. She agreed to a one-year deal with the Wings during the offseason but will have plenty of competition for playing time in the backcourt from Paige Bueckers, Arike Ogunbowale and Azzi Fudd. The 33-year-old Sims remains an intriguing late-round fantasy pick for 2026, but she carries some risk due to her lack of maintaining a consistent roster spot in recent years, and she'll likely have trouble finding consistent minutes as long as her teammates remain healthy.

Carrington spent the first four years of her career in Connecticut but was on the move last year, as she was traded to the Wings ahead of the 2025 campaign before being dealt to Minnesota in early August. Across her 31 regular-season appearances between the two teams, she averaged 9.5 points, 3.6 rebounds, 1.5 assists and 1.1 steals in 20.8 minutes per game, though her playing time decreased after joining the Lynx. Carrington dealt with multiple injuries during her age-27 campaign, including a left mid-foot sprain that forced her to miss the end of the playoffs and the 2026 Unrivaled season. Carrington signed a one-year contract with the Sky during the offseason, but she underwent surgery to address her left foot injury over the winter, and it's not yet clear whether she'll be ready for the start of the 2026 WNBA campaign.

Hines-Allen was a strong fantasy contributor with the Mystics in 2020 and 2021, but she's had mixed results across the past four seasons. After being traded from Washington to Minnesota in 2024, she signed with the Wings ahead of the 2025 campaign and saw slightly increased opportunities in Dallas, averaging 7.6 points, 6.0 rebounds and a career-high 2.9 assists in 22.1 minutes per game across 40 regular-season appearances (20 starts). While her scoring remained relatively steady, her averages in rebounds and minutes were her best marks since 2021. Hines-Allen was an unrestricted free agent during the offseason and elected to sign with Indiana, where she could take on a prominent role in a frontcourt that lost Natasha Howard this spring. Hines-Allen has proven she can be a solid fantasy option when given enough opportunities, and she should have the opportunity to compete for a featured role with her new team.

Rice spent four seasons at UCLA and showed improvement in most areas as a senior to help lead the Bruins to a national title. She was the sixth overall pick in this year's draft and will join one of the league's newest franchises in Toronto. Despite her improvements at the collegiate level in the 2025-26 campaign, Rice joins a Tempo roster that acquired several capable guards ahead of its inaugural season, including Marina Mabrey, Brittney Sykes and Julie Allemand, who was selected with the second overall pick in the expansion draft. As a result, Rice could see limited opportunities during the 2026 WNBA season and instead focus on developing alongside the team's veterans. While Rice has ample talent, she may not see enough minutes to be a reliable fantasy contributor as a rookie.

Despite making a career-high 43 appearances, including 14 starts, with the Mystics in 2025, Dolson put up career-low numbers across the board, save for her injury-riddled 2023 season in New York. When playing 20-plus minutes, Dolson has been a strong fantasy contributor in her career, but she'll have plenty of competition for minutes in 2026 after signing with the Storm. Although Seattle lost Nneka Ogwumike and Skylar Diggins during the offseason, the team retained Ezi Magbegor and Dominique Malonga while drafting Awa Fam at No. 3 overall. Dolson's draft-day value will be limited if she's unable to claim a starting role, but the 34-year-old center could see slightly more work than usual early in the year since Magbegor is slated to miss the start of the season due to a right foot injury. Dolson's role could shrink throughout the season once Magbegor returns to full health and Malonga and Fam develop. However, Dolson is a player to watch early in the season in case she can carve out a fantasy-relevant role in Magbegor's absence.

Fiebich served primarily as a three-and-D presence on a loaded Liberty roster in 2025. She started all of her 37 regular-season appearances, though she was far from one of the team's primary scoring options. Fiebich averaged 8.7 points, 3.5 rebounds, 1.7 assists and 1.4 three-pointers in 28.1 minutes per game, knocking down 42.5 percent of her three-point attempts. She ranked fourth in the league in three-point percentage, but Fiebich's role doesn't appear to be in for an increase in usage with stars Sabrina Ionescu, Breanna Stewart and Jonquel Jones expected back with New York for 2026, while the Liberty also acquired Satou Sabally during the offseason. The lack of steady usage might render Fiebich an inconsistent fantasy option once again, though she still has some appeal as a late-round flier or streaming candidate.

Hiedeman enjoyed a productive second season with the Lynx, finishing second in Sixth Player of the Year voting while averaging 9.1 points, 2.8 assists, 1.9 rebounds and 0.7 steals in 18.9 minutes per contest over 44 regular-season games. She was highly efficient, especially after the All-Star break, averaging 11.1 points on 54.2 percent shooting from the field and 48.4 percent shooting from downtown across 19.5 minutes per game in the final 20 regular-season games. The 29-year-old guard has come off the bench for the majority of her career but signed with the Storm during the offseason, and she could have an opportunity to take on a leading role in Seattle's backcourt this year, making her an intriguing fantasy option.

Amoore sustained a right ACL injury during a training camp practice last season and underwent season-ending surgery before her rookie campaign even began. With the 2025 No. 6 overall pick sidelined, her fellow rookies, Kiki Iriafen and Sonia Citron exploded onto the scene. Iriafen and Citron are expected to lead a new-look Mystics squad this season, but Amoore, who was a full go during preseason action, figures to be a key piece of Washington's youth movement, which added Lauren Betts, Angela Dugalic and Cotie McMahon in the first round of the 2026 WNBA Draft. Given her recent injury, it wouldn't be surprising to see the Mystics monitor Amoore closely this season, and as an undersized guard, she may struggle against professional competition. However, Amoore was an elite playmaker in college, with a knack for jumping passing lanes and irritating opposing ballhandlers. There are certainly question marks when drafting Amoore in fantasy, but the potential upside is enticing in the later rounds.

Burke parlayed a minor breakout 2025 campaign with the Liberty into a one-year deal with the Sun, where she started Connecticut's preseason opener and scored 13 points in 21 minutes. The 29-year-old forward averaged career highs across the board last season, posting 8.1 points, 2.4 rebounds, 1.3 assists and 0.8 steals in 24 games while shooting 49.6 percent from the field and 47.5 percent from beyond the arc. However, a right calf strain cost her a couple of weeks. Burke's three-point shooting was a revelation in 2025 after years of inconsistency from distance, and if that efficiency carries over, she could carve out a meaningful role in Connecticut's rotation. The concern is that the Sun already have plenty of established options competing for minutes, including fellow newcomer Brittney Griner, which could cap Burke's upside. She's best viewed as a late-round dart throw in fantasy drafts, with most of her value likely coming as a streaming option during weeks when Connecticut's schedule is favorable or when injuries open up additional playing time.

Hull set career highs across the board during her fourth season in the WNBA (all with Indiana), but her increased production had a lot to do with how many injuries the Fever sustained in 2025, namely Caitlin Clark missing 39 games (including postseason play). Hull was a restricted free agent during the offseason, but Indiana officially reached a deal to bring her back in 2026. Given her steady contributions during a tumultuous campaign, it wasn't surprising to see the Fever retain her. However, Indiana also retained Kelsey Mitchell, Sophie Cunningham and Aliyah Boston while bringing in Myisha Hines-Allen, which could make it difficult for Hull to eclipse the career-high marks in starts (30) and minutes per game (27.0) that she set in 2025.

The Sun extended a restricted qualifying offer to Nelson-Ododa during the offseason and ultimately reached a deal to bring her back for 2026. The 25-year-old center spent the first four years of her career in Connecticut and will remain with the club following a career-best 2025 campaign. Over 37 regular-season appearances, including a career-high 21 starts, she averaged 8.2 points, 5.0 rebounds, 1.2 blocks, 0.9 assists and 0.7 steals in 21.6 minutes per contest. While she has yet to make much of an impact in the assists column or from beyond the arc over her career, Nelson-Ododa showcased her defensive chops last season. She could provide fantasy managers with solid center stats if she has enough opportunities, though she'll have to share some work with Brittney Griner in the frontcourt.

After a promising rookie season in 2024, Edwards struggled to begin 2025 and was traded to the Sun. With Connecticut in the midst of a rebuild, Edwards' playing time may be prioritized, but in 15 appearances with the Sun last year, she averaged only 4.6 points, 4.2 rebounds and 0.9 steals in 17.0 minutes per game. This is an important year for Edwards' future in Connecticut, as the club has an option for 2027 before she'd become a restricted free agent in 2028. If she can carve out a starting role or play 20-plus minutes off the bench in 2026, she should be a solid pick in the middle rounds of fantasy drafts, but given her regression as a sophomore and Connecticut's offseason acquisition of Brittney Griner, Edwards is certainly a risky selection.

The No. 12 pick in the 2025 WNBA Draft, James was thrust into a major role in the middle of the season due to injuries. From June 20 through July 13, James averaged 14.4 points, 4.2 rebounds, 2.9 assists and 1.1 steals in 30.9 minutes per game. However, outside of this stretch, she never strung together consecutive games in double digits. James could carve out a consistent rotational role in Year 2, but she'll have plenty of competition for minutes since the Wings brought back Arike Ogunbowale and drafted Azzi Fudd first overall to play alongside Paige Bueckers.

Fagbenle was selected by the Valkyries in the WNBA Expansion Draft ahead of the 2025 campaign and took on a sizable role with Golden State. The 33-year-old averaged career highs in points (7.4), rebounds (4.9), assists (1.6), steals (0.9) and minutes per game (23.7) across 39 regular-season appearances, including 38 starts. Fagbenle was an unrestricted free agent ahead of the 2026 season, and she'll join another franchise its first year after agreeing to a one-year contract with the Tempo. She'll likely have the opportunity to retain a significant role with Toronto, which makes her an intriguing fantasy options in the mid-to-late rounds heading into 2026.

After several years away from the WNBA, Allemand returned to the league with the Sparks in 2025 and made a career-high 34 appearances (27 starts) while averaging 5.4 points, 5.0 assists and 3.7 rebounds in 28.3 minutes per game. She was selected by the Tempo with the second overall pick in the WNBA Expansion Draft this spring, and head coach Sandy Brondello said that she expects Allemand to begin the season in a starting role. Allemand has experience in a starting role, as she also exclusively started in her 22 regular-season appearances with the Fever in 2020, but she could still be the third option in Toronto's backcourt behind Marina Mabrey and Brittney Sykes. Allemand's starting role makes her an intriguing pick in the mid-to-late rounds of fantasy drafts, but the talent around her could slightly limit her impact.

Whitcomb saw a substantial decline in production with the Storm in 2024, but she bounced back in 2025 after signing with the Mercury. She served as a part-time starter and averaged 9.1 points, 2.6 rebounds, 2.5 assists and 2.0 made three-pointers in 23.9 minutes per game across 43 regular-season appearances (20 starts). The 37-year-old maintained a decent fantasy floor for most of the year but had some inconsistent stretches over the second half of the campaign. She re-signed with the Mercury ahead of the 2026 campaign and could have to settle for a part-time starting role once again, but she's still a solid threat from the perimeter and will likely have the chance to see relatively consistent playing time.

As a rookie in 2022, Engstler averaged a career-high 18.2 minutes per game for the Fever. However, since then, she's played limited roles for Minnesota and Washington, averaging fewer than 15 minutes per game in each of the past three years. While she averaged double-digit minutes during her two years in Washington, her production was modest, and she started only three of her 72 regular-season appearances. This offseason, she was selected in the first round of the 2026 WNBA Expansion Draft by the Fire. Engstler was Portland's fourth pick, and while the team added a few other forwards ahead of the regular season, the prioritization of Engstler in the draft suggests she'll play a major role in 2026. She has a clear path to a career-high campaign in terms of playing time and production, but her overall skill set remains limited, lowering her fantasy ceiling.

McMahon transferred to Ole Miss for the 2025-26 campaign after three productive seasons at Ohio State and had stellar production for the Rebels while seeing time as a point guard, averaging 19.5 points, 5.1 rebounds, 3.0 assists and 1.1 steals in 30.0 minutes per game. She served exclusively as a starter during her time in college but is joining a roster with several intriguing young options after being selected by the Mystics with the No. 11 overall pick in this year's draft. McMahon plays with plenty of speed and physicality and has developed a perimeter shot across the past two seasons. It wouldn't be surprising to see her have to settle for a reserve role as a rookie, but she could provide a spark off the bench and carve out additional minutes as the season progresses.

Okot played just two seasons at the collegiate level, as she handled a starting role for Mississippi State in 2024-25 and showed improvement after transferring to South Carolina for the 2025-26 campaign, averaging 12.8 points, 10.6 rebounds, 1.4 blocks and 1.3 steals in 23.3 minutes per game. She'll join Atlanta in 2026 after the Dream selected her with the No. 13 pick in the draft, and the 6-foot-6 center will provide size for the team after Brittney Griner departed during the offseason. Despite Griner's departure, the Dream have enough talent in Allisha Gray, Rhyne Howard, Angel Reese and Brionna Jones that Okot won't need to make an immediate impact in the WNBA and can instead focus on developing. Okot will be able to learn from the abundance of veteran talent around her in 2026, but she likely won't have consistent enough opportunities to provide much fantasy value in redraft leagues.

Burrell has played mainly off the bench during her time in the WNBA, but she's seen her production increase in each of the last three seasons. Most recently, she averaged 7.5 points, 2.3 rebounds and 1.2 assists in 18.4 minutes per game across 28 regular-season appearances (one start) with the Sparks in 2025. She's profiled mainly as a streaming option during her four-year career, but she established a relatively high floor last year and warrants late-round consideration ahead of the 2026 campaign. The 25-year-old received a reserved qualifying offer from Los Angeles in April, so the Sparks had exclusive negotiating rights with her, and she'll officially remain with the team in 2026. While she's seen her role grow in recent years, her usage in 2026 will depend on how the minutes are distributed between Burrell, Erica Wheeler, Julie Vanloo, Ta'Niya Latson and Sevgi Uzun behind Kelsey Plum and Ariel Atkins.

McCowan's fourth season in Dallas didn't go as expected. After starting 38 of her 39 regular-season appearances in 2024, the 29-year-old center averaged career lows in points (5.6), rebounds (4.6) and minutes per game (12.9) in 2025. She appeared in 17 regular-season games before being waived in early August and will search for a new home ahead of the 2026 campaign. McCowan has the ability to provide value as a scorer, rebounder and shot blocker but will need to land in a situation where she's given the minutes to do so.

After averaging over 20 minutes per game in four consecutive seasons, Allen saw just 18.7 minutes per game with the Sky in 2025 with averages of 5.1 points and 2.6 rebounds, both of which were her lowest marks since the 2018 campaign. She also started in less than half of her regular-season appearances for the first time since 2019, but she did appear in every regular-season matchup for the second time in the past three seasons. The 33-year-old was an unrestricted free agent ahead of the 2026 season and agreed to terms with the Liberty, but she may not see enough opportunities to bounce back this year, especially since the team also brought in Satou Sabally while retaining Breanna Stewart, Jonquel Jones and Leonie Fiebich. Allen had some strong fantasy performances last year but also had some disappointing outings due to her inconsistent usage, making her a risky pick in the later rounds of fantasy drafts.

Banham began the 2024 campaign with Connecticut before being traded to Chicago, where she averaged several career highs during her first full season with the team in 2025. Over 44 regular-season appearances (33 starts) last season, the 32-year-old guard averaged career-best marks in points (9.0), assists (2.7), three-pointers (2.0), steals (0.6), blocks (0.3) and minutes per game (24.6), shooting 38.2 percent from the field and 35.7 percent from three-point range. She's a career 37.0 percent shooter from downtown, which helps her fantasy appeal, though Banham could have trouble generating considerable fantasy upside while competing for minutes behind Skylar Diggins, Courtney Vandersloot, Jacy Sheldon and DiJonai Carrington after agreeing to remain with the Sky for the 2026 season.

Johnson helped lead South Carolina to the Final Four in four of her five seasons with the Gamecocks, and she'll link up with former South Carolina teammate Aliyah Boston in Indiana after being selected by the Fever with the No. 10 overall pick in this year's draft. Johnson put forth one of the best seasons of her collegiate career during the 2025-26 campaign, averaging 9.9 points, 5.1 assists, 4.0 rebounds and 1.5 steals in 28.6 minutes per game. She could have time to develop as a rookie in the WNBA since the Fever already have a talented roster that includes Boston, Caitlin Clark and Kelsey Mitchell, which limits Johnson's fantasy appeal in redraft leagues.

Nurse served mainly as a starter in three of her first four WNBA seasons, but she's had to settle for a part-time starting role across the past three years. The 30-year-old has had relatively consistent production across those three seasons despite playing for three different teams in Seattle, Los Angeles and Chicago, averaging 6.9 points, 2.1 rebounds and 1.3 assists in 20.6 minutes per game. Availability hasn't been a concern for Nurse, who has appeared in every regular-season game in three consecutive seasons, and she's able to contribute in multiple areas. She's a somewhat high-floor, low-ceiling fantasy option who should be considered with late-round picks in most fantasy formats, but managers should be prepared to use her as a streaming option, especially if she's used as a part-time starter once again after agreeing to terms with the Tempo.

During her first two years in the WNBA, Martin has been a serviceable streaming option in deeper fantasy leagues, but her inconsistent role and production have capped her upside. Last season, she averaged 6.2 points, 2.7 rebounds and 1.0 assists in 16.4 minutes per game, with her value spiking when she got hot from three. Martin scored a career-high 21 points against the Liberty on June 25, but she also had eight scoreless outings and finished in single digits 23 times. She's started only six of her first 76 regular-season appearances in the WNBA and will likely be buried on Golden State's depth chart in 2026, making her minutes sporadic. While a low-priority asset on draft day, Martin should be a hot waiver-wire pickup if injuries hit Golden State's backcourt.

After a breakout season in 2023 in which Sutton averaged 8.2 points, 4.8 assists and 2.6 rebounds in 26.3 minutes per game across 40 regular-season appearances (12 starts) with the Mercury, Sutton took a step back in 2024 while playing for Phoenix and Washington. However, she bounced back in 2025 following a full offseason with the Mystics, and she averaged 7.4 points, 3.9 assists and 1.8 rebounds in 26.1 minutes per game while serving exclusively as a starter. The 27-year-old will have another change of scenery this year after being selected by the Fire in the second round of the WNBA Expansion Draft. Sutton should be in the mix for meaningful minutes with Portland, but the Fire selected several other promising guards, so she carries some fantasy risk heading into 2026, especially since the team also acquired guards Maya Caldwell and Haley Jones via free agency.

Dugalic is a strong shooter and a versatile defender with size, but she could be brought along slowly as a rookie after being drafted by the Mystics with the No. 9 pick in the 2026 WNBA Draft. Dugalic joins a roster filled with young talent, including UCLA teammate Lauren Betts, who was drafted by Washington at No. 4 overall. After serving mainly as a starter during the 2023-24 and 2024-25 seasons with the Bruins, she came off the bench in 35 of 38 appearances during the 2025-26 campaign, but she remained productive, averaging a career-best 9.0 points to go with 5.6 rebounds, 2.2 assists and 1.1 steals in 23.8 minutes per game. Even if Dugalic is forced to come off the bench early in her WNBA career, she's proven that she can make an impact as a reserve, though her fantasy upside in 2026 may be limited.

Gustafson put herself on the fantasy radar with the Mercury in 2023 by averaging 7.9 points and 3.9 rebounds in 15.1 minutes per game, but she was much more inconsistent with the Aces across the past two seasons, averaging 3.4 points and 1.9 rebounds in 11.0 minutes per game during 58 regular-season appearances (eight starts). She missed the first several weeks of the 2025 campaign due to a lower-leg injury, and she wasn't a consistent part of the Aces' rotation down the stretch. She was an unrestricted free agent ahead of the 2026 campaign and ultimately decided to join Portland, where she should compete with Luisa Geiselsoder for minutes at center, but Gustafson could have to settle for a bench role with her new team.

Although Clark made 15 starts across 42 regular-season appearances between the Sparks and Mystics in 2025, she struggled to maintain a consistent fantasy role, averaging 4.0 points and 3.0 assists in 20.4 minutes per game. Her scoring average was her lowest mark since her rookie season in 2012, while her rebound average was her lowest since 2014. The 38-year-old was an unrestricted free agent ahead of the 2026 campaign and elected to join the Wings on a one-year deal, where she'll presumably play behind Alanna Smith and Maddy Siegrist. There are likely other players with more upside available later in fantasy drafts, so Clark profiles mainly as a streaming candidate heading into 2026.

Following four dominant seasons at Utah, Kneepkens transferred to UCLA for the 2025-26 campaign and helped lead the Bruins to a national title. She was selected by the Sun with the 15th overall pick in the draft, capping off a first round in which a record-breaking five UCLA players were chosen. Kneepkens' shot volume declined during her season at UCLA, but she's a versatile shooter, which should allow her to carve out playing time with the rebuilding Sun. Across her five collegiate seasons, she averaged 14.8 points, 4.4 rebounds and 2.4 assists in 27.5 minutes per game, and she should have opportunities to develop the aspects of her skill set outside of shooting as part of a roster that has plenty of young talent. Kneepkens' scoring abilities prop up her fantasy value, but her potential inconsistent playing time in 2026 makes her more appealing as a streaming option.

Onyenwere started 40 games over the past two seasons for Chicago but joined the Mystics on a multi-year contract during the offseason. In five WNBA seasons, she's made 182 regular-season appearances (97 starts) with three different teams, so Onyenwere figures to be in the mix for a consistent role alongside Kiki Iriafen in Washington's frontcourt. While a steady contributor, she's never finished a season as a top-50 fantasy option, so managers shouldn't reach for her on draft day, even if she earns a starting role with the Mystics. However, she's a safe late-round pick who should definitely be on radars throughout the season.

Talbot is a 31-year-old forward with eight years of WNBA experience across six different teams. After getting waived by Golden State in July last season, she signed with New York and served as a depth option, averaging 12.4 minutes per game with meager numbers of 2.5 points, 2.2 rebounds, 1.5 assists and 0.5 steals. Her production was volatile, as injuries to Breanna Stewart, Nyara Sabally and Kennedy Burke boosted Talbot's usage at times, giving her occasional flashes of fantasy value. Talbot was an unrestricted free agent during the offseason and elected to join another contender in Las Vegas. Her hit-or-miss nature and limited floor make Talbot a low-upside pick on draft day, but she could be a valuable streamer during the 2026 campaign if the Aces deal with injuries at some point.

Brown had a career-best season in her return to the WNBA with the Wings in 2023, averaging 7.8 points and 4.5 rebounds in 16.4 minutes per game across 32 appearances (five starts). However, she hasn't had as much playing time over the past two years, averaging 5.4 points and 3.5 rebounds in 13.0 minutes per game across 68 regular-season appearances (three starts) between Dallas and Phoenix over the past two years. Brown had trouble maintaining a spot in the Mercury's rotation down the stretch in 2025, and while she remained under contract with Phoenix ahead of the 2026 campaign, she agreed to a contract buyout with the Mercury in mid-April and will be able to seek out other opportunities. Assuming she lands another roster spot, she could have some productive stretches in 2026 but profiles mainly as a streaming option in most fantasy formats.

McDonald was waived by the Sparks ahead of the 2025 regular season but landed a hardship contract with the Fever in early June. She was waived less than two weeks later, though the 26-year-old guard ultimately signed a rest-of-season pact with the Fever in late June due to Caitlin Clark's persistent left groin injury. McDonald appeared in 20 regular-season games (13 starts) before her season was cut short by a broken bone in her right foot, finishing with averages of 9.8 points, 4.7 assists, 2.4 rebounds and 1.3 steals while shooting a career-high 42.9 percent from the field in 26.3 minutes per game. McDonald then appeared in just one Unrivaled game in 2026 before being ruled out for the remainder of the season with a right lower extremity injury, and it's unclear whether she'll be available to begin the 2026 WNBA season, and her fantasy value will depend on her health and where she signs as an unrestricted free agent.

Evans' availability to start 2026 is in question after she was ruled out of the Unrivaled playoffs with a left lower extremity injury, and the Aces announced in mid-April that she'll be sidelined indefinitely. When healthy, the 27-year-old proved to be a reliable bench spark for Las Vegas in 2025, appearing in all 44 regular-season games while averaging 6.6 points, 2.2 assists and 1.1 rebounds in 17.7 minutes per game. Her modest numbers limit her season-long appeal, but she's flashed upside, including a 21-point, four-steal performance during Game 1 of the WNBA Finals. However, those outings are rare given her reserve role behind Jewell Loyd and Chelsea Gray. Evans is best treated as a deep-league streaming option, whose value hinges entirely on her health and role. After winning a ring in Las Vegas, Evans re-signed with the team during the offseason, but it's not yet clear when she'll be able to suit up in 2026.

After a career-low season in New York, Harrison was an unrestricted free agent ahead of the 2026 campaign but joined the Tempo on a one-year deal during the offseason. The veteran has been a regular top-100 fantasy option throughout her career despite never playing a major role, so Harrison should be on fantasy radars in case she can carve out minutes after competing with Temi Fagbenle, Nyara Sabally and Aaliyah Nye during training camp. However, while consistent, Harrison has never been an elite producer, so managers shouldn't reach for her on draft day. She's a safe late-round pickup and solid streamer whenever she's playing 20-plus minutes. During the seven games in whichshe played at least 17 minutes in 2025, Harrison averaged 10.9 points, 3.9 rebounds, 1.7 steals and 1.1 assists in 18.3 minutes per game.

Uzun finished the 2025 season with the Sky, posting 3.7 points, 2.7 assists and 1.4 rebounds in 18.7 minutes across 18 appearances (three starts). She received a reserved qualifying offer from the Sky during the offseason but ultimately joined the Sparks on a training camp contract. However, she'll have plenty of competition for playing time behind Kelsey Plum and Ariel Atkins, as Uzun will likely compete with Rae Burrell, Erica Wheeler, Julie Vanloo and Ta'Niya Latson for minutes. Uzun is a solid role player, but without an elite trait, she's not guaranteed major usage. With Dallas in 2024, Uzun was a top-100 fantasy option after appearing in all 40 regular-season games and making 19 starts for an injury-ravaged Wings squad, but she seems unlikely to play a similar role in Los Angeles in 2026.

Angloma has had a successful season overseas in France for BLMA, averaging 15.5 points, 5.7 rebounds, 2.3 assists and 1.3 steals in 29.2 minutes per game, and she was selected 12th overall by the Sun in this year's draft. The 19-year-old is a stellar finisher and possesses versatility that could allow for her to carve out opportunities for a rebuilding Connecticut squad early in her WNBA career, but she'll need to develop her outside shooting to complement her athleticism. Angloma has the tools to be successful in the WNBA, but she'll likely have her workload managed in 2026 as she works on developing with the Sun.

Harris had a strong season with Connecticut in 2024, averaging a career-best 10.5 points and 3.0 assists in 28.8 minutes per game across 39 regular-season outings (38 starts). She was traded to the Wings during the offseason but dealt with an early-season knee injury that ultimately required surgery and ended her year after just five appearances. She signed with the Fever during the offseason, and her knee procedure isn't expected to impact her availability for the start of the 2026 season. Harris wasn't much more than a streaming candidate in fantasy prior to 2024, and she could have trouble carving out a role behind Caitlin Clark, Kelsey Mitchell and Lexie Hull in Indiana's backcourt. She's worth a late-round flier in deeper fantasy formats, but she could have a somewhat low floor while presumably operating as a reserve.

Mair had a productive freshman season at Boston College but transferred to Duke for the final three years of her collegiate career. Her production initially took a step back with the Blue Devils, but she showed considerable improvement in 2025-26, averaging 11.6 points, 5.9 rebounds, 5.6 assists and 2.5 steals in 33.9 minutes per game. Mair is an effective playmaker who improved as a shooter and defender during her senior season at Duke. The Storm selected her 14th overall in the 2026 WNBA Draft, and while Seattle is expected to be a rebuilding team this year, Mair's opportunities as a rookie will likely depend on whether she can build upon the momentum of her 2025-26 performance at the collegiate level. Although the Storm lost several key contributors during the offseason, they still have plenty of talented players, including fellow 2026 first-rounders Awa Fam and Flau'jae Johnson, so Mair's playing time could be inconsistent this year.

Martin has professional experience in Europe and was selected by the Fire with the No. 7 overall pick in this year's draft. However, she dealt with an illness during international play and wants to focus on getting healthy and playing for Spain in the FIBA World Cup in September, so she intends to stay in Spain for the 2026 campaign before coming to the WNBA in 2027. Martin is a point guard who is proficient in the pick-and-roll with strong abilities as a passer, but fantasy managers will need to wait until next year before considering her in redraft leagues.
